# Product framing

**Target user.** Students and early-career analysts who want to move into data engineering.

**Career pathway.** Data Engineer and closely related roles (analytics engineer, data platform engineer, ETL engineer and data warehouse engineer).

**Industry.** Insurance carriers, NAICS 5241. These are the companies that sell and underwrite insurance policies.

**The question the product answers.** Which skills make someone the most qualified for a Data Engineer job at an insurance carrier, and which of them pay off?

# Limitations

The product gives a student a grounded starting point but it does not yet do the following things well.

- **The Data Engineer sample is small.** Only 29 postings matched our strict Data Engineer definition and only 13 of them list a salary. The market snapshot and skill gap describe those 29 jobs. The salary model uses the wider set of 395 distinct insurance data jobs because 29 is too few to model.
- **One company shapes the results.** State Farm posted 15 of the 29 Data Engineer postings. UnitedHealth Group (with its Optum unit) and Humana posted the largest share of the wider salary sample.
- **Advertised pay is not offered pay.** Salaries come from postings that chose to list one. The model explains about 37% of pay differences between jobs and its typical miss on new jobs is about $21,000.
- **The model shows association and not cause.** Cloud skills go with higher advertised pay but part of that may come from the better-paying teams that ask for cloud.
- **Skill ratings are self-reported.** The team's 1 to 5 ratings were not checked by a test so the skill gaps are development signals and not measures of job readiness.
- **The data is one year from one industry.** All results come from 2024 postings at insurance carriers and may not hold for other industries or later years.
